title: DSPy: The End of Prompt Engineering - Kevin Madura, AlixPartners
talk_summary: A consultant demonstrates DSPy as a declarative Python framework where typed signatures/modules replace hand-written prompts, with adapters controlling prompt formatting and optimizers (GEPA/MIPRO) auto-tuning prompts against metrics. Most value comes from the programming abstractions, not the optimizers; the one concrete cost lever is optimizing a small/cheap model to recover accuracy lost versus an expensive one.

takeaways.technique: Optimize cheap model to recover accuracy of expensive model
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the optimizer against a small/cheap model on the same task+metric so its prompt is tuned to close the gap with the big model, then serve the cheap model.
takeaways.numbers: Example: 4.1 ~high accuracy -> 4.1-nano ~70% -> optimized back to ~87% (illustrative, not measured in talk)

takeaways.technique: Metric-driven prompt optimization (GEPA/MIPRO) with small datasets
takeaways.what_they_do: Define typed inputs/outputs plus a scoring metric, then let an LLM-driven optimizer iteratively rewrite the prompt against 10-100 labeled examples, saving the compiled program.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as long as you have enough, maybe 10 to 100 of inputs and outputs... the improvement can be pretty significant.

takeaways.technique: Typed signatures as the prompt contract
takeaways.what_they_do: Declare inputs/outputs as typed fields (Pydantic-like); field names and docstrings become the prompt, and structured output is enforced and parsed automatically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the names of the fields themselves act almost as like mini prompts. It's part of the prompt itself.

takeaways.technique: Swap prompt-format adapters (JSON vs BAML) without changing program
takeaways.what_they_do: An adapter layer formats the same signature into different prompt encodings; a more compact/readable format can improve accuracy and token efficiency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: can actually improve performance by you know five to 10 percent depending on your use case.
takeaways.numbers: 5-10% performance improvement cited (third-party testing, not measured here)

takeaways.technique: Per-call model override via context manager
takeaways.what_they_do: Set a global default LM but override it for specific calls (e.g., route image work to Gemini, reasoning work to a big model) inside the same program.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if I detect an image, I will route the request to Gemini. If I detect something else, I'll route it to a 4.1

takeaways.technique: Recursive chunked summarization for long documents
takeaways.what_they_do: Split long documents into chunks, summarize each with a signature, then summarize the summaries to fit context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we'll go through as many pages as there are. We'll do some uh basically recursive summarization
